#9648. Vendor Lock-In Is Creating a Market for Escape

Co-founder of Gale Strategies, a marketing and public relations firm serving technology companies and tech investors.

Co-founder of Gale Strategies, a marketing and public relations firm serving technology companies and tech investors.

Co-founder of Gale Strategies, a marketing and public relations firm serving technology companies and tech investors.

Jeff Bezos famously said, “Your margin is my opportunity.” Where incumbents carried generous margins and sought rents, a hungry challenger saw room to win by serving customers better and charging less. Today, the line could be, “Your switching costs are my opportunity.” A new wave of enterprises is building a business out of jailbreaking customers from platforms.

And “platform” used to be a positive word. Investors liked platforms. Customers liked them too. And the latter dependably picked a platform over an agglomeration of best-in-class solutions. Our own little outfit is no exception. Maybe you weren’t excited about the platform over the best in class alternative. But the platform application fit with every other platform application better, and the combined cost and security were and remain seductive.

Well, the security may remain seductive. But the pricing is changing.

We have lived this at our own firm. ActiveCampaign notified us that our monthly plan would move from $295.29 to $399.46 on December 19th, an increase of about 35%, with the new rate applying unless we completed cancellation before that date. ActiveCampaign's price increases stem from a multi-year shift from simple email marketing to an all-in-one, AI-powered automation platform.

But putting that aside, its last raise was in 2021, the peak of the zero-interest-rate tech bubble. Venture capital and growth-equity funds like those that put their then-cheap money into the company typically look for an exit within five to seven years. So it’s time to monetize the switching costs developed over that period. Essentially firms like ours whose contacts and CRM intelligence are in the platform. But to the extent that money is being put into improving the platform, it’s not easy to see.

The market is also saturated, and smaller firms like ours require proportionately more handing than large enterprises for less revenue, so we’re no longer welcome unless we’re willing to pay closer to what big companies are seeking to pay. We’re not going to get better service out of this price increase, but large enterprises might.

Anyone who has read about the history of redlining in the U.S. and how places like Harlem paid for America’s suburbs will start to get aspects of the picture, though in an exponentially more insidious and morally corrupt form. Not to pick on ActiveCampaign, because despite their attempting to mollify us by inviting us to pay a little bit less in absolute terms by paying it all in advance, they’ve been accommodating enough about letting us get off here, and us letting them try to focus on the large enterprises.

With Cision - our reporter database and wire service platform - we had stayed through earlier price increases even though the service wasn’t delivering anything new or better that we wanted. We did this because we assumed that in exchange for our loyalty they would help us out if we needed it.

As we’ve pursued a pivot, we asked for help with the cost. They couldn’t give us any, and we gave notice of non-renewal. We then learned that services couldn’t be removed mid-contract and they were bent on holding us down. While previously it was just the reporter database we wanted to address, now we’ve realized that while we saw them as a partner who would reward loyalty, the company is actually a risk and can amplify and compound problems if and when they occur. So we are now moving off both of their services. We’re also looking more carefully at the ownership structure and financing of the tech solutions and platforms we use, because we don’t want our data and workflows in the hands of an outfit that must monetize its switching costs on that same five-to-seven-year clock.

Neither vendor lost us over a feature or poor service. The products were great, exactly what we needed. Though interestingly in both cases once we left the platform we realized we had been missing superior services from competitors or we could just build what we needed internally. It wasn’t a priority to find alternatives, but both companies made it one for us, and we have benefited, as have our own clients.

This is the problem with switching costs as a competitive advantage.

The more a company raises prices, no matter how much it claims the increases fund improvements the customer doesn’t recall asking for, the more the switching costs become a bitter experience. As one operations leader said within earshot of me recently, “I hate platforms, I don’t want us to be on a platform.” And as the cheap money becomes scarce, and U.S. policymaking does that it has been doing in very recent years, that sentiment is likely to increase.

Vertice, a software-procurement firm that tracks what its customers pay, reports preliminary SaaS inflation of 14.3 percent in September 2026, after a record 16.4% in June. Over the same twelve months, US consumer prices rose 3.7 percent according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI release of October 14th. Vertice’s figure is a vendor-published average drawn from its own customer base, not an official statistic. But Microsoft’s own pricing announcement shows the pattern at the largest platform, effective July 1st Microsoft 365 Business Basic rose from $6 to $7 per user per month. That’s 16 percent. Business Standard went from $12.50 to $14 So 12 percent. And Microsoft 365 E3 has gone from $36 to $39 for 8 percent. Existing customers move to the new prices at renewal.

When a software company loses confidence that it can win customers by building better products, it stops trying to keep customers because they love the product. It tries to keep them because they can’t leave.

Challenger, Gray & Christmas counted 171,501 announced US technology job cuts through October 2026. That is up 21 percent from a year earlier and already more than the 154,445 for all of 2025. Layoffs.fyi lists about 149,000 tech employees laid off at 366 companies worldwide so far this year. Companies increasingly say AI is the reason. The evidence for that is thin.

Challenger has tracked AI as the most-cited reason for layoffs for several months running in 2026, but laid-off workers describe something else. In a February 2026 Gallup survey of more than 23,000 US workers, only about 1 percent of those laid off said AI directly caused their job loss. Most cited restructuring, cost-cutting and economic conditions, and that includes a shift away from customer-centrism to rent-raising. A study reported by Fortune in August 2026 foud some of the companies studied cut staff before investing much in AI, allegedly to free up money for it. Revelio Labs found that companies announcing AI-driven layoffs had actually been adding AI talent more slowly than their industry peers, at a median of about 11 percent over two years compared with more than 13 percent. Forrester estimates that only 6 percent of US jobs will be automated by 2030. If AI were doing the work of the people being let go, these numbers would look different.

The layoffs line up better with a change in where companies want their people. Support and product engineering are shrinking. Sales, account management and migration programs are protected or growing. And prices are rising on customers who find it hard to leave.

Start with Broadcom and VMware. VMware had more than 38,000 employees at the start of 2023 and about 16,000 two years later, according to Business Insider. Smaller customers lost direct support and were routed to a distributor, with response times stretching to a week or more. European cloud providers documented price increases of 800 percent to 1,500 percent. Even so, a January 2026 CloudBolt survey of 302 IT decision-makers found that only 4 percent had fully replaced VMware. Untangling the dependencies typically takes 18 to 24 months. The study concluded that Broadcom is deliberately accepting customer churn while maximizing margins on the customers who remain. Support quality was a top concern for 78 percent of respondents, and 85 percent expect further price increases. None of this depends on AI.

Broadcom ran the same playbook after buying CA Technologies in 2018, and Constellation Research analyst Ray Wang said when the VMware layoffs began that this is how Broadcom makes money from its acquisitions.

At Salesforce, CEO Marc Benioff claimed in September 2025 that AI agents had allowed the company to cut its customer support workforce from about 9,000 to 5,000. He says he has held engineering headcount flat at roughly 15,000 for two years. In January 2026 he said the company was hiring 20 percent more account executives. In August 2025, Salesforce raised prices on Enterprise and Unlimited editions of Sales Cloud, Service Cloud and other products by an average of 6 percent, after a 9 percent increase in 2023. AI is harder to accept as the explanation, given that Business Insider reported Agentforce usage remained relatively low and the product hadn’t matched the company’s demos. In early 2026, Salesforce cut roles on the Agentforce team itself.

In May 2026 Cloudflare eliminated more than 1,100 positions, about 20 percent of its workforce, in the same period it reported record quarterly revenue of $639.8 million, up 34 percent. Its executives said AI use had increased more than 600 percent in three months and that employees were running thousands of AI-agent sessions a day. If AI had been driving the decisions, you would expect the heaviest AI users to be protected, but according to reporting on the earnings call, the company protected salespeople carrying revenue quotas instead, and the cuts reached across every other team and geography.

In January 2026 Amazon announced 16,000 corporate job cuts, following 14,000 in October 2025. Washington state filings show the largest category was software development engineers, along with security, data and quality-assurance engineers, applied scientists, UX designers and product managers. Amazon described the cuts as removing layers and bureaucracy. One of those let go was N. Lee Plumb, his team’s head of AI enablement, whom Amazon had flagged as one of the top users of its AI coding tool, Kiro, by his account, only five people in the company used it more. A company replacing people with AI would have little reason to let him go.

SAP’s 2024 restructuring affected about 10,000 roles and cost €3.1 billion. Its CFO said the goal was to decouple expenses from revenue growth. The same year SAP created a board-level unit dedicated to moving customers to the cloud. Mainstream support for its ECC system ends in 2027, and SAP has said future innovation, including AI, will be available only in the cloud. Senior executives surveyed by Constellation Research described its RISE migration program as financial engineering more than a benefit to customers.

Regulators have documented how hard it is for customers to leave. In November 2024 the US Government Accountability Office found that five of six federal agencies it interviewed had run into restrictive vendor licensing practices. Three were required to buy again licenses they already owned in order to run that software in the cloud. One had to pay to regain ownership of its own data when a contract ended. In July 2025 the UK Competition and Markets Authority concluded that switching between cloud providers was extremely rare and that egress fees and licensing practices were hurting competition. It estimated that prices just 5 percent above competitive levels would cost UK customers about £500 million a year in a market of roughly £10.5 billion.

AI gives these companies a forward-looking explanation for cuts that investors reward. The pattern underneath appears more prosaic. Vendors may be cutting the engineers and support staff who understand the customer’s problems. They are putting their headcount and money into the sales teams, migration programs onto platforms with switching costs and contract structures that move customers onto their platforms and keep them there. And they appear to be raising prices on customers whose cost of leaving keeps rising. Customers get less help, pay more and have fewer ways out in this formulation.

Enterprise software used to win by building a better product, solving harder problems and giving customers a reason to renew. Today a vendor can do well by building an ecosystem customers can’t easily leave, cutting the cost of serving them and charging the installed base more. Engineering then gets judged by how efficiently the vendor makes money from the customer’s dependence.

CIOs and CFOs evaluating a cloud migration or AI rollout may want to look past this year’s budget savings and ask whether the vendor’s product, service and flexibility are improving, or whether their company is just becoming more dependent on a vendor that profits from engineered retention more than satisfaction. A vendor that cuts the engineers who understand its users while protecting the people who lock those users in has stopped competing on product, and its customers usually find that out at renewal.

To execute a pivot toward raw infrastructure rent-seeking, corporate leadership almost always chooses a specific archetype of manager we feel, the platform generalist. These leaders’ core competencies are systems integration (without passing the benefit on to customers), horizontal scaling, and cross-application alliances. They don’t see software as a solution that delivers greater benefits to users, they see it as a distribution channel to force consumption of underlying cloud servers.

And if some feature or pricing model will lure the unsophisticated into the trap, this manager is willing to be rewarded for it, trading integrity for short-term margin and a hoped-for getaway when the market catches on.

Under this framework, specialized, domain-rich product teams are systematically trimmed or ignored to fund massive infrastructure buildouts. This creates an organizational environment of intellectual debt, the company stops asking how to innovate to save its users time, and starts asking what the bare minimum is to prevent a total customer revolt.

When a company reaches this stage, it stops creating value and starts extracting rent, it weaponizes its legal departments, licensing audits, and predatory contract bundles to squeeze extra margin out of a captive customer base, and product excellence gives way to operational coercion.

The fatal flaw in the rent-seeking playbook is the assumption that your moats are made of stone, when they are actually made of code and human expertise.

When an organization defunds its application layer to buy database chips, for instance, it inevitably triggers a catastrophic brain drain. The elite domain specialists, the institutional anchors who spent decades perfecting niche compliance features, complex calculation logic, and granular user workflows, realize there is no longer a seat for them at the table. They leave. Sometimes it’s worse: bad strategy leads companies to escort their best people out the door as they pivot away from the user and toward servicing their debt covenants.

Losing a superstar domain specialist is not just an HR headache; it is a structural breach in the corporate moat. Even if the individual is deep inside the org and you think the customers can’t see them, other team members can, and they get the message: caring about the user and customers is not rewarded here, and it’s time to get out while you still can. These specialists you’re losing possess a rare dual capability: they understand the hyper-complex, real-world problems of the industry, and they know exactly where the legacy software’s seams are weak. When an executive lets an elite product leader and engineer walk out the door, they lose their translation shield, and with it the internal credibility required to keep customers from rebelling against an unusable interface.

More importantly, they give the open market a weapon. In the modern cloud landscape, enterprise lock-in is ultimately just a data mapping problem. The moment an elite architect leaves and teaches rival platforms or cloud-flexible competitors how to untangle, translate, and automate the migration of your proprietary code, the “divorce-proof” illusion evaporates.

This is where Hamilton Helmer’s book 7 Powers is instructive. He names switching costs as one of the seven sources of durable competitive advantage, and the most deceptive of them. Switching costs are the one ring that rules them all, they make you feel powerful because people are forced to stay with you, even against their will.

But like the ring, the power corrupts the one who wields it. Once you lose your customers’ will, and they must stay with you without choosing you, you have already lost. You are no longer earning loyalty; you are guarding prisoners. And a new wave of enterprises is attacking exactly that vulnerability.

The customer’s side of the trap looks a lot like asking the Mafia for a favor. The first offer is generous: a bundled discount, free migration credits, a deal that solves today’s problem. It feels like a friendship. Only later do you learn the favor was never a transaction; it was a debt, and the debt has no payoff date. Every renewal comes with new terms, and every attempt to leave is met with a reminder of what you owe. You didn’t buy a product; you accepted a relationship you can’t exit.

The more a business or investor falls into its own trap, using switching costs to save itself and squeeze customers and clients, the more hated it becomes. Even those who stay are like the subjects of a Soviet regime, compliant on the surface, waiting for their chance to escape or overthrow it. When that chance arrives, they take it.

This is why switching costs are a toxic, addictive, and self-destructive power to lean into. The more you use it for short-term returns, the more you sacrifice the trust and authenticity on which long-term persistence is best built.

The tragedy of the platform generalist is that financial metrics often shield them from reality until it is too late. Because enterprise data gravity is heavy and moving off a core utility layer is a multi-year, multi-million-dollar risk, revenue may continue to climb for years on forced renewals alone.

Coming back to VMware under Broadcom returns to a test case. Broadcom’s infrastructure software segment, which includes VMware, reported $6.9 billion in revenue in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, up 19 percent from a year earlier. AT&T alleged in a 2024 lawsuit that Broadcom proposed a 1,050 percent increase to its annual VMware bill. The case was settled out of court.

Customers have been slow to leave, however. The CloudBolt survey cited earlier, of 302 IT decision-makers at North American companies with at least 1,000 employees, found that 86 percent were actively reducing their VMware footprint even though only 4% had fully migrated off it. That is the illusion in numbers, revenue climbs on forced renewals while customers plan their exit. CloudBolt sells hybrid cloud management software, so treat its survey as indicative rather than definitive.

But a company that takes an anti-customer approach and sells to anti-customer gatekeepers has written its own obituary. It becomes an empire built on quicksand. Modern organizations, the startups, high-growth scale-ups, and developers of the next generation, will avoid these legacy utilities like the plague. They build on open, flexible, product-led architectures designed to remain rent-proof from day one.

The lesson for modern tech leaders may be absolute, infrastructure means nothing if the software on top of it is unusable or beige as one revenue leader in professional services and tech said recently.

If you strip your company of its product-deep soul to fund a commoditized infrastructure floor, you are not building a permanent monopoly. You are handing agile, user-first challengers a highly profitable opening to deliver a clean-break data blueprint and hollow out your captive customer base from the outside. You might win the budget war today, but you have guaranteed your long-term irrelevance.

A simple test, can you say upfront that what you are selling is handcuffs? If, instead, you are selling how cool-looking and comfortable the handcuffs are, you are losing. Your switching costs are someone else’s opportunity, and they are coming for it.

Platform lock-in is now big enough to support its own escape industry.

Nutanix added 3,000 new customers in fiscal 2026, its third straight year at that pace, and much of that growth came from customers leaving VMware. Red Hat stripped the container features out of OpenShift to give VMware users a product that runs only virtual machines. It says the number of VMs running on that platform grew 417 percent in a year and that its services team has assessed more than 1.46 million VMs for migration. HPE became, in Forrester’s words, the first hardware vendor to build its own virtualization software in response to Broadcom’s takeover of VMware.

Many of the people building this escape industry learned the trade inside the platforms customers are now trying to leave. VergeIO, which sells a VMware replacement and recently sped up its migration tools, put former VMware CTO Kit Colbert on its board and hired Parag Patel, a former VMware sales vice president, as CEO. About 19,000 people have left VMware since Broadcom took over. KORE1 says the largest share is landing in the migration practices of system integrators such as Accenture, Deloitte, Kyndryl and HCLTech. A single exit can absorb a team. KORE1 estimates Western Union’s migration of 900 to 1,200 applications needs 30 to 50 engineers. The pattern reaches past VMware. Rimini Street says its primary support engineers average more than 20 years of experience. Dreamteam, founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million for an AI-native CRM and has already replaced Salesforce at DMS Health.

At the end of the day, where do you invest into your own tech capabilities, both as an individual advancing your career, or as an enterprise leader or investor? The Jailbreak economy is looking promising.

Also, apologies to Thin Lizzy fans for the headline.

The Boutique PR Firm Is Having Its Moment

Co-founder of Gale Strategies, a marketing and public relations firm serving technology companies and tech investors.

#9647. I Audited All 143 KB of 328K-Star obra/superpowers: Fewer Hallucinations, or 3x Your Token Bill?

Every coding feed is calling obra/superpowers (328K+ GitHub stars, MIT) a must-install upgrade for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity.

Instead of repeating the hype, I inspected all 15 SKILL.md files (143,103 bytes total) in the repository to see what it actually instructs your agent to do.

Superpowers is not a runtime wrapper. It is a strict software-engineering rulebook injected into your agent across 16 supported clients.

On multi-file refactors or greenfield modules, this drastically lowers thrashing and broken assumptions.

Open the largest file in the repo — subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md (19.7 KB) — and look at line 12:

Core principle: Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec compliance + code quality) + broad final review

For every single small task, the workflow dispatches an implementer subagent, a spec-compliance reviewer, and a code-quality reviewer, followed by a final whole-branch review.

On a trivial 2-minute CSS or API timeout fix, that ceremony stretches wall-clock time to ~10 minutes and pushes token usage 2.8x to 4.0x higher than a direct vanilla prompt.

#9644. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.

#9642. Ahrefs vs SEMrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Use?


SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.

If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.

In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.

What is SEMrush?


SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.

The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension

Features

  • Most accurate keyword data: Accurate keyword search volume data is crucial for SEO and PPC campaigns by allowing you to identify what keywords are most likely to bring in big sales from ad clicks. SEMrush constantly updates its databases and provides the most accurate data.
  • Largest Keyword database: SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool now features 20-billion keywords, providing marketers and SEO professionals the largest database of keywords.

  • All SEMrush users receive daily ranking data, mobile volume information, and the option to buy additional keywords by default with no additional payment or add-ons needed
  • Most accurate position tracking tool: This tool provides all subscribers with basic tracking capabilities, making it suitable for SEO professionals. Plus, the Position Tracking tool provides local-level data to everyone who uses the tool.
  • SEO Data Management: SEMrush makes managing your online data easy by allowing you to create visually appealing custom PDF reports, including Branded and White Label reports, report scheduling, and integration with GA, GMB, and GSC.
  • Toxic link monitoring and penalty recovery: With SEMrush, you can make a detailed analysis of toxic backlinks, toxic scores, toxic markers, and outreach to those sites.
  • Content Optimization and Creation Tools: SEMrush offers content optimization and creation tools that let you create SEO-friendly content. Some features include the SEO Writing Assistant, On-Page SEO Check, er/SEO Content Template, Content Audit, Post Tracking, Brand Monitoring.

Ahrefs



Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The company was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.

Features

  • Backlink alerts data and new keywords: Get an alert when your site is linked to or discussed in blogs, forums, comments, or when new keywords are added to a blog posting about you.
  • Intuitive interface: The intuitive design of the widget helps you see the overall health of your website and search engine ranking at a glance.
  • Site Explorer: The Site Explorer will give you an in-depth look at your site's search traffic.
  • Domain Comparison
  • Reports with charts and graphs
  • JavaScript rendering and a site audit can identify SEO issues.
  • A question explorer that provides well-crafted topic suggestions

Direct Comparisons: Ahrefs vs SEMrush

Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.

User Interface

Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.

In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.

AHREFS



The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.

Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include:

  • You can see analytics from the dashboard, including search engine rankings to domain ratings, referring domains, and backlink
  • Jumping from one tool to another is easy. You can use the Keyword Explorer to find a keyword to target and then directly track your ranking with one click.
  • The website offers a tooltip helper tool that allows you to hover your mouse over something that isn't clear and get an in-depth explanation.

SEMRUSH



When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic.

You'll also find some other options like

  • A search bar allows you to enter a domain, keyword, or anything else you wish to explore.
  • A menu on the left side of the page provides quick links to relevant information, including marketing insights, projects, keyword analytics, and more.
  • The customer support resources located directly within the dashboard can be used to communicate with the support team or to learn about other resources such as webinars and blogs.
  • Detailed descriptions of every resource offered. This detail is beneficial for new marketers, who are just starting.

WHO WINS?

Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.

When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.

Rank Tracking

If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.

Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.

Ahrefs



The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.

Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:

You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.

It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.

SEMRUSH



SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:

All subscribers are given regular data updates and mobile search rankings upon subscribing

The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.

Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.

Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.

WHO WINS?

Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.

SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.

Keyword Research

Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you plan on using for future content rather than those you use now.

When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms.

AHREFS



The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine.

Ahrefs supports several features, including:

  • It can search multiple keywords in a single search and analyze them together. At SEMrush, you also have this feature in Keyword Overview.
  • Ahrefs has a variety of keywords for different search engines, including Google, YouTube, Amazon, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex, and other search engines.
  • When you click on a keyword, you can see its search volume and keyword difficulty, but also other keywords related to it, which you didn't use.

SEMRUSH



SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear.

The Keyword Magic Tool also lets you to:

  • Show performance metrics by keyword
  • Search results are based on both broad and exact keyword matches.
  • Show data like search volume, trends, keyword difficulty, and CPC.
  • Show the first 100 Google search results for any keyword.
  • Identify SERP Features and Questions related to each keyword
  • SEMrush has released a new Keyword Gap Tool that uncovers potentially useful keyword opportunities for you, including both paid and organic keywords.

WHO WINS?

Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike.

If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations.

Competitor Analysis

Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you.

AHREFS



Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more.

Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have.

To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours.

SEMRUSH



SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including:

Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites.

SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more.

The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets.

WHO WINS?

SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.

Pricing

Ahrefs

  • Lite Monthly: $99/month
  • Standard Monthly: $179/month
  • Annually Lite: $990/year
  • Annually Standard: $1790/year

SEMRUSH

  • Pro Plan: $119.95/month
  • Guru Plan:$229.95/month
  • Business Plan: $449.95/month

Which SEO tool should you choose for digital marketing?

When it comes to keyword data research, you will become confused about which one to choose.

Consider choosing Ahrefs if you

  • Like friendly and clean interface
  • Searching for simple keyword suggestions

  • Want to get more keywords for different search engines like Amazon, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex, Baidu, and more

 

Consider SEMrush if you:

  • Want more marketing and SEO features
  • Need competitor analysis tool
  • Need to keep your backlinks profile clean
  • Looking for more keyword suggestions for Google

Both tools are great. Choose the one which meets your requirements and if you have any experience using either Ahrefs or SEMrush let me know in the comment section which works well for you.

#9641. How Scan to Win Assured Cashback Works Under the Hood: Single Use QR Codes at Scale

Product QR cashback is everywhere in India now: scratch the hidden panel on a pack, scan, and money lands in your wallet. It looks simple from the outside. Under the hood, a scan to win assured cashback campaign is a small security system that has to stop reuse, guessing, and counterfeit packs, while still responding in under a second.

Here is how a system like Assured Rewards approaches the problem, and what any developer building something similar should think about.

Each pack gets a unique code. If codes are sequential, someone will script through them. So:

The code is printed under a scratch panel so it cannot be read on the shelf. That matters: without it, anyone in the store could photograph codes and redeem them before the buyer gets home. The QR on the outside can carry the campaign and batch, while the hidden part carries the secret.

The core rule is simple: one code, one reward. Two people scanning the same code at the same second must not both get paid.

If zero rows come back, the code was already used or never existed. Both are useful signals.

A code that does not exist, or one that was already redeemed in another city, is often a sign of a fake or copied pack. Log the location, device and time of every failed scan. Clusters of failures around one distributor or market are exactly what a brand's anti counterfeit team wants to see. This is why the same scan that pays cashback also works as a genuine product check.

Crediting a bank account directly on every scan is slow and expensive. A better pattern:

A good scan to win campaign feels instant and generous to the buyer, and boring and predictable to the finance team. Secure code generation, atomic redemption, a ledger based wallet and solid fraud rules are what make assured cashback possible. If you want to see the consumer side of this flow, Assured Rewards is a live example of QR cashback with genuine product verification and UPI withdrawal.

#9639. Sellfy Review 2022: How Good Is This Ecommerce Platform?

Are you searching for an ecomerce platform to help you build an online store and sell products?

In this Sellfy review, we'll talk about how this eCommerce platform can let you sell digital products while keeping full control of your marketing.

And the best part? Starting your business can be done in just five minutes.

Let us then talk about the Sellfy platform and all the benefits it can bring to your business.

Sellfy is an eCommerce solution that allows digital content creators, including writers, illustrators, designers, musicians, and filmmakers, to sell their products online. Sellfy provides a customizable storefront where users can display their digital products and embed "Buy Now" buttons on their website or blog. Sellfy product pages enable users to showcase their products from different angles with multiple images and previews from Soundcloud, Vimeo, and YouTube. Files of up to 2GB can be uploaded to Sellfy, and the company offers unlimited bandwidth and secure file storage. Users can also embed their entire store or individual project widgets in their site, with the ability to preview how widgets will appear before they are displayed.

Sellfy is a powerful e-commerce platform that helps you personalize your online storefront. You can add your logo, change colors, revise navigation, and edit the layout of your store. Sellfy also allows you to create a full shopping cart so customers can purchase multiple items. And Sellfy gives you the ability to set your language or let customers see a translated version of your store based on their location.

Sellfy gives you the option to host your store directly on its platform, add a custom domain to your store, and use it as an embedded storefront on your website. Sellfy also optimizes its store offerings for mobile devices, allowing for a seamless checkout experience.

Sellfy allows creators to host all their products and sell all of their digital products on one platform. Sellfy also does not place storage limits on your store but recommends that files be no larger than 5GB. Creators can sell both standard and subscription-based products in any file format that is supported by the online marketplace. Customers can purchase products instantly after making a purchase – there is no waiting period.

You can organize your store by creating your product categories, sorting by any characteristic you choose. Your title, description, and the image will be included on each product page. In this way, customers can immediately evaluate all of your products. You can offer different pricing options for all of your products, including "pay what you want," in which the price is entirely up to the customer. Sellfy is ideal for selling digital content, such as ebooks. But it does not allow you to copyrighted material (that you don't have rights to distribute).

Sellfy lets you integrate it with your existing website using "buy now" buttons, embed your entire storefront, or embed certain products so you can reach more people. Sellfy also enables you to connect with your Facebook page and YouTube channel, maximizing your visibility.

Sellfy is a simple online platform that allows customers to buy your products directly through your store. Sellfy has two payment processing options: PayPal and Stripe. You will receive instant payments with both of these processors, and your customer data is protected by Sellfy's secure (PCI-compliant) payment security measures. In addition to payment security, Sellfy provides anti-fraud tools to help protect your products including PDF stamping, unique download links, and limited download attempts.

To expand functionality and make your e-commerce store run more efficiently, Sellfy offers several integrations. Google Analytics and Webhooks, as well as integrations with Patreon and Facebook Live Chat, are just a few of the options available. Sellfy allows you to connect to Zapier, which gives you access to hundreds of third-party apps, including tools like Mailchimp, Trello, Salesforce, and more.

Sellfy has its benefits and downsides, but fortunately, the pros outweigh the cons.

Victoria, Seychelles, November 27th, 2026/Chainwire/--The BASIS Card returns money differently. Announced today by BASIS DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE LTD, the payment card credits cashback in the asset used for each eligible purchase, with Platinum cardholders qualifying for 10% cashback during the introductory Launch Boost period.

For digital asset holders, the principle is straightforward. Spend Bitcoin and receive Bitcoin back. Pay with Ethereum and receive Ethereum back. There are no reward points to redeem or proprietary platform tokens to manage. Cashback is credited in an asset the cardholder already uses, giving everyday spending a direct connection to their digital asset holdings.

The opening of first-round applications marks an expansion of BASIS's existing digital asset infrastructure into everyday payments. Applications are submitted at https://basis.pro/card and close on December 31, 2026, at 23:59 UTC.

The BASIS Card is available in Standard, finished in matte black composite, and Platinum, produced in metal. Applicants select their preferred edition when submitting their waitlist application, with qualification determined by their active staking position.

Each edition has a separate staking eligibility threshold, as detailed below. BASIS measures the value of the applicant's active staking position against the requirement for their selected tier. The position is assessed at submission and re-checked at the close of the application period.

Participants can therefore review the benefits of each edition alongside its staking requirements before deciding which card to apply for. Final issuance remains subject to the issuing partner's independent review.

Both editions feature an introductory Launch Boost period, beginning on the date of card issuance. During this period, cardholders receive enhanced cashback rates, higher monthly reward caps, and additional subscription benefits.

*All monetary figures are expressed in USD. Physical card issuance fees include applicable shipping charges.

Launch Boost runs for three months following issuance, after which each card returns to its respective base benefits. Standard and Platinum also feature rate-lock periods of 12 and 24 months, respectively, subject to the applicable program terms.

Along with cashback, the card program brings together subscription rebates of 50% or 100%, depending on the edition and benefit period, across a catalog of over 80 subscriptions. Travel and additional card benefits include two annual airport lounge visits, a 3 GB eSIM, and one additional card, subject to tier eligibility and applicable terms. Standard cardholders benefit from a 2% FX fee, while Platinum cardholders pay no FX fee during Launch Boost. Both editions provide immediate access to a virtual card upon activation, with Platinum participants also receiving priority and dedicated support.

The defining feature of the BASIS Card is what happens after a purchase. Where conventional reward programs may require cardholders to accumulate points or convert rewards into their preferred currency, BASIS keeps the cashback denomination consistent with the asset spent.

Cashback on eligible settled purchases is credited directly to the cardholder's Funding Wallet. A purchase made using BTC returns BTC, leaving the recipient free to decide how to use the reward.

Cardholders who wish to stake their cashback can do so separately under the platform's ordinary conversion rules. Cashback does not automatically enter an existing staking position, and card rewards remain independent of staking yield.

Submitting a card application also leaves existing staking positions, lock-up periods, Dynamic Reward Rates, boosters, and stToken balances unchanged.

Applications are free and limited to one per account during Round 01. Participants must hold at least USD 1,000 in eligible BASIS wallet value at submission, maintain an account in good standing, and satisfy the staking requirements for their selected card edition.

Once BASIS approves a waitlist application, the applicant receives further instructions and a secure Know Your Customer (KYC) verification link. The issuing partner then conducts its own review, covering identity verification, residency, regional eligibility, sanctions screening, and supporting documentation.

Waitlist approval permits applicants to proceed to the next stage and does not constitute final card approval, activation, or issuance.

Further information on card eligibility, benefits, fees, and application requirements is available in the official BASIS Card Program documentation.

Sounds like you're biased for Grammarly. Not really that informative if you're already leaning towards one to begin with. Still, it was an interesting read. Tell me, do you use Grammarly with your day-to-day writing/blogging?

I use the paid versions of both Grammarly and Pro Writing Aid. Both of them have issues:- Grammarly IS more focused on nonfiction than fiction. If you're writing fiction, you may find Grammarly's insistence on "Conciseness" annoying. They seem to want to take the soul out of your writing, which is fine for a corporate report or technical manual, but not for your Great American Novel.- Grammarly pushes features on users that are not ready for prime time. It doesn't matter that you never agreed to be a beta tester for them; you get to do it anyway.- Pro Writing Aid actually counts the occurrences of words in your document and tells you when a word has been overused compared to published literature. Grammarly, on the other hand, seems hell-bent to remove certain words that it has deemed overused from the language, whether or not they're actually overused in your document.- Grammarly's Clarity function is simply horrible. It mangles sentences and changes their meaning. Sometimes the result of its suggestion is unintelligible garbage.- Grammarly allows you to turn off some checks, but not all of them. Unfortunately, the ones you cannot turn off are some of the most irritating (such as that horrible "Clarity"). On the other hand, Pro Writing Aid lets you choose which checks you use.- Pro Writing Aid has a mediocre command of American English (it's a British product). The app insists on rules of grammar and spelling that are outright wrong, per Merriam-Webster, the Chicago Manual of Style, and modern usage as shown by Google Books Ngram. At one point, Pro Writing Aid insisted that American English did not include the words "holiday" and "autumn," that "vacation" and "fall" must be used instead.- Pro Writing Aid's rules for commas are 100 percent consistent with the way I learned them in high school--50 years ago! They do not reflect modern usage. Grammarly is much better at this.- Pro Writing Aid seems to waste their limited resources on tweaking their UI. Their UI most definitely could use improvement, but these changes are not great improvements; they only serve to confuse users. Their resources would be better spent fixing the many functional problems in their app.- Some of Pro Writing Aid's checks are completely useless, as they do not take context into consideration. For example, an ordinary word would not be capitalized as part of a narrative, but would be as part of a title (for example, "professor." But if you capitalize correctly for context, Pro Writing Aid dings you for "Inconsistent capitalization." Similar issues exist with hyphenation consistency check.Each of these applications has its strengths as well as considerable weaknesses. I will say that both of them are light-years better than the execrable grammar checker in Microsoft Word, but that's damning with faint praise.

#9630. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9626. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9625. How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later.

The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions.

Ryan from our Baker’s Hotline is here with the answer.

You sure can! It will still work the next time you want to bake. But remember, as with any dairy product, there are always precautions to take.

The USDA recommends keeping butter at room temperature for no more than two days to prevent spoilage. Salt is a preservative and can lengthen the shelf life, but for the sake of this article, we’re talking about unsalted butter. (It’s more appropriate for baking and is the type called for in most King Arthur recipes.)

“If the butter has only been on the counter at room temperature for a few hours or overnight and has maintained a temperature below 70°F, it should be just fine to place back in the fridge,” says Ryan. “You may not notice a difference in the performance of the butter when you eventually use it, other than the wrapper being a bit wet or soft. Food safety-wise, it’s still good to use.”

“If the butter became very soft or started to melt during its time on the counter (or in the microwave if you were speeding up the process), you can put it back in the fridge, but it may not be the best to use in your recipe,” Ryan suggests. “You may notice when it solidifies that it’s separated or grainy. The water, fats, and solids in butter are an emulsion, which can break when melted and re-solidified.” If your recipe depends on butter to create air or structure, like a cake that calls for creaming butter and sugar, you’ll want to start over with new butter.

“If you used that butter in a recipe requiring creaming, the air you incorporate wouldn’t be as stable since the structure of the butter has changed,” Ryan says. “Your baked goods may not rise properly, and frostings may be soft and loose. Is it still safe to use? Food safety-wise, yes. But structure-wise, perhaps not.”

That butter can still be used for other things though! Extra-softened or even melted and re-solidified butter will still work perfectly to spread on toast or pancakes, to be made into brown butter, or to remelt and use in recipes calling for melted butter like a Graham Cracker Crust.

If your butter has been unrefrigerated for more than two days, you run the risk of it going rancid. As Ryan says, “There is no coming back from rancid butter.” It has a distinctly unpleasant flavor and a noticeable rancid smell that carries over into baked goods. It’s best to dispose of the butter if this happens.

But what if you want to keep your butter at room temperature for days at a time to slather on your morning toast? Ryan recommends storing your butter in a butter keeper if you want to leave it on the counter. “The water in the base of the jar creates an airtight seal, helping prevent the butter from spoiling. So long as it is stored away from direct heat and light, the butter in a container like this will be fine for a few days. Be sure to replace the water often and clean the container before filling again.”

“When working with butter in a recipe, I like to bring out and soften only the amount that is needed for what I am working on. That way, I don’t end up with extra butter that won’t be used right away,” he says. “Repeatedly moving butter from the fridge to the counter and then back invites spoilage and poor performance.”

In a rush? To soften your butter more quickly, Ryan advises, “Cut your butter into pats and place them on a plate in a single layer at room temperature. More surface area means that the butter will soften a bit faster!”

The number one reason side businesses fail is not lack of funding, bad timing, or tough competition — it is building something nobody wants to buy. Before you spend a dollar on a website, business cards, or inventory, you need to validate that real people will pay real money for what you are offering.

Validation does not require a perfect product. It requires proof of demand. Talk to 10 people who match your target customer. Describe what you plan to offer. Ask two questions: "Would you pay for this?" and "How much would you pay?" If 3 or more say yes with a specific dollar amount, you have a viable idea. If most say "that sounds cool" but hesitate on paying, you have a hobby.

The FI community has a particular advantage here. Many FI seekers have already cut their expenses to the point where a side business does not need to generate massive revenue to make a meaningful impact. Even $500 to $1,000 per month in side business income — invested consistently — can shave years off your FI timeline.

Forget building a $1 million business. Your only goal is reaching $1,000 in total revenue as quickly as possible. That first $1,000 proves three things: people will pay you, you can deliver, and the business model works. Everything after $1,000 is optimization. The FI community calls this the "ramen profitable" stage — your business covers its own costs and generates even a small surplus. From there, you compound both your skills and your revenue.

Side business income is the ultimate FI accelerator because it attacks both sides of the equation. Your day job covers expenses while 100% of your side income goes directly to investments. If your side business generates $1,500 per month and you invest all of it at 7% annual returns, you will have over $450,000 in 15 years. That is not a theoretical number — that is the real math of why thousands of FI seekers build side businesses.

One of the first decisions you face is how to structure your business legally. For most side businesses, the choice is between operating as a sole proprietorship (the default — no paperwork needed) or forming an LLC (Limited Liability Company). Here is the honest comparison.

A sole proprietorship is what you are by default when you start earning money on the side. There is no registration required at the federal level (though you may need a local business license). The income flows directly to your personal tax return on Schedule C. The downside: your personal assets — savings, home equity, investments — are not separated from business liabilities.

An LLC creates a legal separation between you and your business. If someone sues your business, your personal assets are generally protected. Formation costs range from $50 (states like Kentucky and Colorado) to $500 (California charges $800 per year just for the privilege of having an LLC). For most side businesses, an LLC is worth forming once you have paying customers.

Side business income is taxed differently than your W-2 paycheck, and the surprises can be painful if you are not prepared.

Self-employment tax: You pay both the employee AND employer portions of Social Security and Medicare — a combined 15.3% on top of your income tax. On W-2 income, your employer covers half. On side business income, you cover it all.

Quarterly estimated taxes: The IRS expects you to pay taxes as you earn, not once a year in April. If you owe more than $1,000 in taxes from side business income, you need to file quarterly estimated payments (Form 1040-ES) by April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15.

Deductions that reduce your tax bill: Home office (simplified method: $5/sq ft up to 300 sq ft = $1,500 deduction), internet (business percentage), equipment, software subscriptions, mileage ($0.76 per mile in 2027), health insurance premiums (if self-employed), and retirement contributions (Solo 401k allows up to $75,000/year). These deductions are a significant FI advantage because they reduce both income tax AND self-employment tax.
